stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec. Cross-platform live preview (GO, UP, MX) is a complex real-time feature requiring full elaboration (openspec) followed by testability, security, and edge-case hardening (speckit).

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a new capability — no existing preview mechanism found. The central attachment point is useContent, which all 236 Contentstack consumers flow through. Injecting preview data there propagates to every consumer without per-component changes. useContent source was not included in the CodeGraph output, so the locationHint is inferred from the blast-radius data (236 callers, every Contentstack component uses it).

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so I authored the full list from the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three-site scope (GO, UP, MX), and openspec's architectural note identifying useContent as the central injection point for 236 consumers. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: I could not read the four referenced files (useContent.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, ContentstackLink.tsx), so these criteria are based on the story description and standard Contentstack live-preview behavior. Criteria may need refinement once actual code structure is known — for example, Contentstack's live-preview SDK may provide specific event shapes, polling mechanisms, or hash-based routing that would change how AC-3 (real-time updates) should be worded. I also noted the case-variant filename (contentstackContext.tsx vs ContentstackContext.tsx) across sites, which could cause import issues if not handled consistently.

Both agents operated blind — openspec inferred the injection point from blast-radius metadata, and speckit authored acceptance criteria from the story title and standard Contentstack behavior without any code-level verification. While both agents added non-overlapping value (openspec: architectural injection-point analysis; speckit: AC authoring and case-variant filename flagging), the spec work is built on unverified assumptions. The case-variant filename observation (contentstackContext.tsx vs ContentstackContext.tsx) across sites is a valid concern but was not confirmed against the repository. A human reviewer must: (1) verify all four file paths exist at their stated locations, (2) confirm useContent is actually the central attachment point with 236 consumers, (3) validate that speckit's blind-authored acceptance criteria match the actual Contentstack live-preview SDK capabilities and event shapes, and (4) resolve the case-variant filename inconsistency.
